analysis_sections.text: The graph-filtered view keeps aspects of the head and facial layout visible beneath a coarse, banded redistribution of appearance. The adjacent original crop shows the actual eyelid and mouth position. Reading the views together helps separate a transformed representation from a visible scene observation. The reconstruction illustrates the spectral perspective; its block-like texture alone does not identify a production method or an editing defect.
analysis_sections.title: A transformed view of the same face

analysis_sections.text: In the middle displayed pair, the strongest positive readout is at the lower viewer-left grid edge, with additional positive and negative values elsewhere. Other sampled pairs have different patterns. The spatial distribution matters: the central attention region does not contain every feature supporting the classifier. These readouts decompose the model margin, so they should not be interpreted as visible boundaries or a diagnosis of a particular facial defect.
analysis_sections.title: Where the classifier readout supports its decision

analysis_sections.text: The unsigned map and connected selection emphasize the central face, including the eye and nose area of the aligned crop. This compact focus differs from the wider contribution pattern. The separate explanation head proposes patch importance from frozen detector features; its output does not replace or reweight the classifier. The fixed region is shared across the clip, making comparisons consistent without providing an independent motion test.
analysis_sections.title: The explanation head’s proposed focus

analysis_sections.text: Only part of the recorded whole-curve comparisons favors the central candidate over the strongest matched controls. The experiments still show how the detector responds when this region is hidden or restored, but they do not qualify it as the unique source of the prediction. The report therefore uses the region to organize inspection while retaining the strong video-level assessment and the broader signed-contribution evidence.
analysis_sections.title: What the selected-region measurements establish

report.conclusion: Detector output can indicate manipulation even when visual inspection reveals no anomalies at given resolution.

diagnosis.evidence_synthesis: No visual manipulation cues were observed in original crops or frame sequences. SSTGNN’s calibrated score favors manipulated, with contribution peaks in facial patches including lower-left and central areas. Regional intervention tests showed mixed curve comparisons and failed fidelity checks, yet the video-level decision stands per policy rules.

inherited_editor_changes.after:
A man in a dark suit and pink shirt appears against a deep red background. The supplied views show changes in gaze, eyelid position and mouth shape. One consecutive window captures an eye closure, while another holds a sideward gaze with small expression changes. The scene is useful for comparing a compact attention proposal with classifier support distributed across the face grid.

SSTGNN strongly favors manipulated. The signed contribution map includes positive support in lower and outer grid locations, whereas the learned attention selection is central. The regional measurements are mixed. The video classification can therefore be described clearly while the selected region remains a proposal for interpreting part of the model response.
inherited_editor_changes.before: A man in a dark suit and pink shirt appears against a deep red backdrop, delivering speech with natural micro-expressions across sparse and consecutive frames. His gaze shifts subtly, eyelids lower and lift, and mouth shapes change smoothly—no visible flicker or discontinuity in the short sequences. The detector assigns an extremely high calibrated fake score, driven primarily by spectral and spatial evidence, while learned attention concentrates on the central facial region. Signed contribution maps show consistent positive support for the manipulated class across multiple grid cells, especially near the nose and upper lip, though no single peak dominates all samples.

This transformed representation carries strong discriminative signal for the classifier, suggesting manipulation may reside in higher-frequency details not visible to the naked eye.
